title: Dizzy Gillespie's small band of the late fifties
summary: Sam describes Dizzy's unrecorded small band with Sonny Stitt, Wynton Kelly, Jimmy Cobb and Candido.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Calling me from South America, you know. So I--after I quit that band, I didn't want no more of that. That was enough of that, man. My nerves was getting ready--then I went in Dizzy's band--Dizzy Gillespie--which was a fine band. This band was--oh, man, and we didn't record not one note. This band with Sonny Stitt, Wynton Kelly and myself, Jimmy Cobb, Candido. This was an excellent band--small band.
Oh yeah? When was this? What year was that?
This was during the same time when Miles had his band.
Oh. Uh huh. Dizzy never recorded nothing.
He didn't record nothing. One note, man. And this was--boy, this band was--
This band was on fire, man.
I know it had to be.
